cards.explanation: The answer is that he calls four kings to help him attack Gibeon. Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sends word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon. His message says, “Come up and help me. We will attack Gibeon…” (Joshua 10:4). He's alarmed, so he does what you do when the group chat is the only plan you've got. Four messages go out, and he's not doing this one alone.

The answer is Joshua in the camp at Gilgal. The men of Gibeon send word to Joshua, Israel's leader, and they say, “Do not abandon your servants. Come quickly and save us!” (Joshua 10:6). That's a message with no small talk in it.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 7 says Joshua and his whole army, including all the mighty men of valor, came from Gilgal. Not a small team and not a few volunteers. When Gibeon calls, the whole army moves, and I think that's one loud parade of sandals.

The answer is that the LORD tells Joshua not to be afraid, because He has handed the enemy over to him. The LORD says, “Do not be afraid of them, for I have delivered them into your hand. Not one of them shall stand against you.” (Joshua 10:8). Five armies are waiting, and the LORD speaks straight to the fear first.

The answer is confusion. Verse 10 says the LORD threw them into confusion before Israel. Joshua had marched all night and caught them by surprise, and then the LORD stepped in too. I think those armies had no idea what hit them.

The answer is False. Verse 11 says the LORD cast down large hailstones from the sky, and more of them were killed by the hailstones than by the swords of the Israelites. I think this part is heavy, so I'll just say it plainly. The hailstones came from the LORD, and the text puts them ahead of the swords.

The answer is the sun and moon to stand still. Joshua speaks to the LORD in front of all Israel and says, “O sun, stand still over Gibeon, O moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.” (Joshua 10:12). That's a big thing to ask out loud with everybody watching. Then the text says the sun stood still and the moon stopped (Joshua 10:13).

The answer is that the LORD listened to the voice of a man. The writer says, “There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, because the LORD fought for Israel.” (Joshua 10:14). The man is Joshua, who had just spoken to the LORD about the sun and moon. The writer says the LORD listened.
